market_specific_notes: Houston neuro-evaluation shoppers usually need a cleaner comparison of testing depth, report usefulness, and adult-versus-child fit instead of generic diagnosis language.
The best local comparison in Houston is whether a clinic explains scope, turnaround, and what the written report is actually for.
local_vetting_points: Ask whether the clinic separates screening, diagnostic clarification, and full neuropsych testing instead of bundling everything into one vague service line.
Ask whether the written report includes practical recommendations for school, workplace, accommodations, or treatment planning.
Ask which age groups the evaluator works with most often and whether autism versus ADHD evaluations are handled differently.
Ask whether follow-up feedback is included or sold as a separate step.
typical_cost_ranges: Houston pricing usually changes based on testing depth, collateral review, scoring time, and report complexity rather than a single flat citywide number.
A low quote is usually less useful if it excludes report writing, feedback, or accommodation-ready documentation.
The clean comparison is total expected cost through report delivery, not just the intake or testing-day number.
payment_options: Ask whether the clinic is private pay only, offers superbills, or helps with reimbursement paperwork.
Ask whether intake, testing, scoring, feedback, and report delivery are billed together or separately.
wait_time_notes: Waitlist reality should be measured across intake, testing date, and report turnaround together.
A fast intake appointment does not mean a fast written report.
If school, work, or accommodations timing matters, ask whether cancellation openings or expedited reporting are real options.
availability_notes: Availability should include adult versus child slots, tele-intake options, and the realistic report turnaround after testing.
Ask whether cancellation openings are common if timing matters.
named_resources_or_providers: Houston-area academic medical centers, psychology networks, and accommodations-oriented provider directories are more useful than generic testing-near-me lists.
Use local specialty fit and report purpose as part of the comparison.
city_intro_override: Houston neuro-evaluation shoppers usually do better when they compare waitlist reality, out-of-network reimbursement, report purpose, and age-fit before they compare marketing claims.

primary_city_decision_block.title: How to choose an autism or ADHD evaluation provider in Houston
items: Ask whether the provider does screening only or a full evaluation with written recommendations.
Ask what the report is actually usable for: school, work accommodations, treatment planning, or diagnostic confirmation.
Ask how long the real timeline is from intake to testing to final report delivery.
Ask whether the clinic accepts insurance, gives a superbill, or expects full out-of-network reimbursement work from you.
Ask whether the evaluator routinely works with adults, children, or both.

testing_scope_notes: Ask whether the clinic offers screening, diagnostic clarification, ADHD-focused testing, autism-focused testing, or a broader differential workup.
Testing depth should match the real decision you need to make.
insurance_reimbursement_notes: Ask whether the clinic is in-network, private pay with superbills, or fully out-of-network with no reimbursement support.
Do not assume testing is covered just because an intake visit is covered.
Ask whether coding, documentation, or superbill language is designed to support reimbursement.
adult_vs_child_fit: Confirm whether the clinician routinely evaluates adults, children, or both, and whether the testing approach changes by age group.
report_turnaround_notes: Ask when the written report is delivered, whether the feedback session is included, and whether accommodations-ready language is part of the standard report.
If the report is needed for school or workplace decisions, ask what usually delays final delivery.
